objective: RC-D: retest EV-AES-e4c091's OUTCOME-A residual limitation U4 -- whether the r=5 yoyo-statistic excess's absence under cipher substitution depended on the substitute being an IDEAL random permutation, or holds also for a deterministic, non-ideal, independently-constructed Feistel PRP.
headline: Both new arms read OUTCOME-A' (the excess does NOT reappear under this structured, non-ideal, deterministic Feistel substitute either): M1 (matched exposure, 2^30 trials) read 0 hits against an analytic null expectation of ~1 and against the frozen r5=14 comparator (p=1.22e-4, ratio CI lower bound 3.32, no upper bound since M1=0); M2 (8x exposure, 2^33 trials) read 9 hits against an analytic null expectation of ~8 (R_point=1.125, 95% CI [0.51, 2.14], CI contains 1) and against the r5 comparator scaled to this exposure (p=1.34e-8, ratio CI [5.02, 32.59] -- far below what a 14-per-2^30-rate excess extrapolated to 8x would predict, ~112 hits). Neither arm shows the elevation the matched live 5-round AES arm shows; both are consistent with their own analytic null and inconsistent with the AES-level rate.

frozen_comparator.note: P1-R5-PAIR (BATCH-009, EV-AES-e4c091 OBS-B9-3) is NOT recomputed here; its reading is read verbatim from the immutable run artifact and used only as a fixed comparator.

construction.kind: keyed, deterministic, fixed-16-round balanced Feistel PRP, 64-bit halves
construction.memory_per_query: O(1) -- direct algebraic evaluation, no stored pair table (unlike BATCH-012's perm128 ideal-permutation architecture, EV-AES-837cd8)
construction.independence_audit: src/INDEPENDENCE_AUDIT.md -- explicit side-by-side against AES's actual S-box/MixColumns/ShiftRows tables and key schedule as implemented in rc8probe.c, and grep-verified zero shared vocabulary with the yoyo_sbox_v2-v4 lineage and rc8probe's own perm128 ideal-permutation code (runs/grep_independence.txt)

exposure_decision.methodology: measured 2^20 smoke and 2^26 timing-calibration arms BEFORE any decisive measurement arm was run; extrapolated linearly; committed to a target only after the extrapolation showed comfortable margin against the remaining wall-clock budget -- per PREREGISTRATION.md section 3.

smoke_2p20.note: sanity check only, hit count not decision-relevant, discarded

exposure_decision.target_reached: 2^30 (M1, matched exposure to BATCH-009's N1/P1 arms) AND 2^33 (M2, 8x exposure, mirroring BATCH-009's own N1/N2 two-level design) -- both reached with wide budget margin, no shortfall relative to BATCH-009's own N1/N2 exposures.
exposure_decision.M1_M2_not_pooled: M2 uses the SAME seed/armid as M1, so M2's trial stream is a superset prefix of M1's (same non-independence class as BATCH-009's own N1/N2, flagged there as EV-AES-e4c091 OBS-B9-5). M1 and M2 are reported and compared to the r5 comparator SEPARATELY below; no pooled M1+M2 statistic is computed.

M2_8x_exposure_2p33.note_on_exposure_mismatch: r5's own comparator (14 hits) was measured at 2^30 trials, not 2^33; this comparison is therefore NOT matched-exposure in the same sense as M1 -- it is the same kind of asymmetric-exposure comparison BATCH-009's own N2-vs-P1 comparison was (EV-AES-e4c091's '8x exposure on the null arm alone' figure), included for the same reason: a higher-precision reading of the substitute arm's own rate, not a claim that r5 was independently re-measured at 2^33.

self_check.note: Before computing any new statistic, the same exact conditional-binomial (Poisson ratio) machinery was run on EV-AES-e4c091's own published (14 vs 1) counts and confirmed to reproduce p=9.77e-4 and ratio CI [2.13, 592] to the precision EV-AES-e4c091 reported, exactly as BATCH-009's own analyze.py self-checked against EV-AES-8b8dcf.

decision_rule_applied.source: Frozen Rank-1 decision rule from PREREGISTRATION.md section 4, itself an exact structural mirror of EV-AES-e4c091's / BATCH-009 TASK-20260803-a0a7b9's own preregistered Rank-1 rule.
decision_rule_applied.OUTCOME_A_prime: the excess does NOT reappear under the Feistel oracle: R's 95% CI contains 1, AND the exact test of r5 against the arm at its exposure gives p<0.01.
decision_rule_applied.OUTCOME_B_prime: the excess REAPPEARS: R's 95% CI lower bound > 1, AND the exact test does NOT reject at p<0.01.

plain_statement: OUTCOME-A (excess absent under cipher substitution) DOES NOT REAPPEAR AS AN EXCESS under this Feistel substitute -- it STAYS ABSENT, exactly as it did under BATCH-009's ideal-permutation substitute. Both M1 (0 hits at 2^30, matched exposure) and M2 (9 hits at 2^33, consistent with the arm's own ~8-hit analytic null) satisfy this task's OUTCOME-A' criterion. This is one additional data point, on ONE fixed 16-round Feistel construction at ONE key, consistent with the r=5 excess NOT being an idealness-specific artifact of BATCH-009's null-object choice -- it also fails to reappear under a deterministic, non-ideal, independently-constructed 128-bit PRP. This narrows U4 for this one construction; it does not resolve U4 for the space of all non-AES deterministic PRPs (see boundaries below), and per the task's own prohibitions this record assigns no evidence strength, no hypothesis status, and recommends no promotion.
boundaries: This is a NEGATIVE result about ONE additional artifact-explanation test for the r=5 excess -- a specific 16-round, murmur3-finalizer-based Feistel PRP -- at one probe geometry (amask=1, smask=1), one key, one seed, trials up to 2^33. It does not generalize to other Feistel round counts, round functions, or non-Feistel deterministic PRP families (residual limitation V4, PREREGISTRATION.md section 1.3).
It does NOT establish that the r=5 excess is real, does not identify a mechanism, and does not support any claim about AES or any cryptographic scheme.

Toy tier only: reduced-round AES-shaped SPN probe geometry, one machine, no crypto-scale, medium-scale, affected-scheme, or asymptotic claim made or implied. No comparison to published cryptanalysis in either direction.

Session and implementation independence only, no model independence: this task, like every task cited above, resolves to one model under standing basis 0137a051eb5828789eb267fa83c8278086578d4c. Nothing here counts toward a closure quorum.

M1 and M2 are NOT independent replicates of each other (same seed/armid; M2's trial stream is a superset prefix of M1's) -- reported and compared to the r5 comparator separately, never pooled, per the precedent EV-AES-e4c091 OBS-B9-5 set.

The M2-vs-r5 comparison is an ASYMMETRIC-exposure comparison (r5 measured at 2^30, M2 at 2^33); it reads M2's own rate more precisely, it does not constitute an independent re-measurement of r5 at higher exposure.

The plaintext-generation code path is asserted (not independently digest-verified against BATCH-009's differently-shaped digest field) to be line-for-line identical in construction to rc8probe.c's worker, with only the oracle calls (enc_r/dec_r bodies) changed -- see PREREGISTRATION.md section 1.3 (V3) for exactly what was and was not verified here.
Thread count differs from BATCH-009's arms (4 here vs 2 there) -- disclosed performance-only deviation, PREREGISTRATION.md section 1.1.
what_was_not_reached: No independent instrument / independent codebase cross-check of this task's own arithmetic or construction was obtained within this task -- unlike BATCH-009 and BATCH-011/012, which had a separate validator re-derive every statistic. This RESULTS.json's statistics were computed once, by this task, using machinery that reproduces EV-AES-e4c091's own published self-check numbers (see self_check block above), but that is not the same as an independent second derivation by a different session/party.

No independently-written second implementation of the Poisson-ratio/Clopper-Pearson machinery was built to cross-check runs/decision_analysis.json's own numbers; the self-check against EV-AES-e4c091's published (14 vs 1) figures is the only cross-check performed.

No second, independently-varied key or seed was run for the Feistel oracle (single key, single seed, matching BATCH-009's own single-key/single-seed design) -- so this task cannot distinguish 'the excess is absent under this construction generally' from 'the excess is absent for this one key.'
No decay check (varying Feistel round count, mirroring BATCH-009's r=10 AES decay-check logic) was run for the new oracle -- FEISTEL_ROUNDS is fixed at 16 for both M1 and M2.

No plaintext-stream digest cross-check against BATCH-009's own P1-R5-PAIR/N1-IDEAL-P30 digest field was performed (different digest formula, disclosed above); byte-identical plaintext generation is a code-inspection claim, not a verified digest match.
